inputs: options-flow-feed-lab.lean=call-heavy (leaning bullish); tickers=12; contractsFlagged=1533; callFraction=0.7406; topPrint=TSLA 360C $116.4M on 12.59x OI
items.method: Cross-read the intraday session type and control against the prior window to detect an auction-character change, then test whether the option-flow premium lean and its most-unusual print are confirmed or contradicted by daily breadth versus the 60% threshold, and overlay the dealer-gamma regime, spot-versus-flip geometry and the VIX band to judge whether an aggressive call-premium bid is being backed by a stable tape or leaning into a fragile, algo-driven one.
items.note: The genuinely new feature this window is a tape-character change into record call premium: the intraday auction has shifted from a balanced range-day under mixed control to a Reversal-risk session under algo-controlled trade with VWAP 765.73 sitting just above spot near 765.41, while option premium is aggressively call-heavy — 1533 contracts clear the $250k bar inside 30 days at a 0.74 call fraction, headlined by a single TSLA 360 call at $116.4M on 12.6x its open interest. Yet the breadth underneath still does not confirm: only 29.99% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day, a 30.01-point shortfall below the 60% broad-participation line, and SPY sits in negative dealer gamma just under the 765.59 flip with VIX easing to 15.31. So speculative call premium is surging into a narrow, algo-reversal tape rather than a broadening one. Watch for breadth to reclaim above the 60% line to validate the bullish premium; the constructive read is invalidated on a daily close below 760.00 on SPY, which would resolve the narrow top downward while the tape is already reversal-prone.
items.title: SPY's intraday auction flipped to a Reversal-risk, algo-controlled tape this window even as call premium surged to 1533 flagged contracts and daily breadth stayed pinned near 30% — record upside premium leaning into a fragile tape

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative dealer gamma; flip=765.59; callWall=770; putWall=765; expectedMove=3.18; spot=765.41
items.method: Read the options-structure gamma sign, flip and wall levels against current benchmark spot, compare the wall-versus-spot geometry and the expected-move width to the prior window to detect compression or a wall shift, confirm the dealer scenario and conviction from the gamma playbook, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP and the VIX band, to judge whether a spot pinned at the flip inside a tightening corridor is coiling to stabilise or merely pausing before the next break.
items.note: The new structural feature this window is a tighter coil with a lifted floor: the near put wall has been raised to 765 from 760 and the front expected move has compressed to plus or minus 3.18 from plus or minus 3.81, so the modelled range has narrowed to roughly 762.2 to 768.6 with SPY spot 765.41 pinned right at the 765.59 flip between the 765 put wall and 770 call wall. Signed dealer gamma is still negative and spot still sits just under the flip, so the market is coiled at the exact level that would flip dealer hedging supportive but has not yet reclaimed it. The gamma playbook still reads range-break-watch with patient conviction, and the intraday auction is now a Reversal-risk session with VWAP 765.73 just overhead, while VIX at 15.31 keeps the band calm. This is a razor-thin coil pinned to the flip with the floor pulled up to 765. Watch a clean reclaim above the 765.59 flip as the trigger that relieves the corridor upward, whereas the constructive read is invalidated on a sustained daily close below 760.00 on SPY, which loses the raised put wall in short gamma and reopens downside toward the lower strikes.
items.title: SPY's dealer put wall lifted to 765 from 760 and the front expected-move band compressed to ±3.18 from ±3.81 with spot pinned at the 765.59 flip — a razor-thin coil at the flip in negative gamma

inputs: sector-research-lab.into=XLE (Leading, accel +4.34); out=XLF (Weakening, accel +1.47); leader=XLV (Leading); benchmark=SPY; count=11
real-assets-lab.scores=ETH-USD 74.2; BTC-USD 71.6; CPER 63.9; PDBC 63.1; DBC 62.8; IBIT 61; GLD 49.7; USO 46.4; SLV 23.6; scored=14; horizon=swing
real-assets-lab.drivers=xle63:8.65; xli63:6.10; btc63:21.69; gld63:1.70; dbc63:2.04; goldSilverRatio63:12.40; breadth:50
items.method: Cross-read the equity sector rotation's into/out legs and their acceleration against the real-assets per-vehicle scores and the 63-day driver block (energy and industrial equity proxies, crypto, gold and the gold/silver ratio), then overlay the benchmark regime and VIX, to judge whether equity leadership and the real-asset drivers are converging on the same cyclical read and whether that cyclical bid is broadening across vehicles.
items.note: The cross-tool feature this window is a broadening cyclical convergence: equity sector rotation is into energy — XLE (Leading, accel +4.34) as XLF weakens (accel +1.47), with XLV still Leading — and the real-asset complex agrees and has firmed. ETH-USD leads at 74.2/100 and BTC-USD 71.6 are both uptrends, industrial copper CPER 63.9, PDBC 63.1 and DBC 62.8 hold firm, gold GLD reads 49.7 and IBIT sits at 61, while silver SLV 23.6 stays weak and oil USO 46.4 is mixed; 14 vehicles scored on a swing horizon. The 63-day driver block reads cyclical — energy-equity proxy +8.65 and industrial-equity +6.10 with the bitcoin proxy +21.69 against a gold proxy of only +1.70 and a broad-commodity proxy +2.04, and a gold-versus-silver ratio proxy of +12.40. So equity leadership and the real-asset drivers both favour the same cyclical energy and crypto risk-on. Watch whether energy and cyclical leadership persist to confirm the convergence; the risk-on read is undercut on a daily close below 760.00 on SPY, which would pull the convergence back toward caution while breadth is still narrow.
items.title: Equity sector rotation into cyclical energy (into XLE, accel +4.34) is converging with a firming risk-on real-asset driver block this window — bitcoin proxy +21.69 and gold GLD 49.7 against weak silver 23.6
